note: P3828 (Pro 6:27) — can a man carry fire in his bosom and his clothes not be burned? (the garment = the self exposed to lust's fire.)

dims.v: the imperilled self — the garment fire inevitably burns
the man who dallies with lust
the man's own person, imaged as clothing that fire in the bosom must consume
the garment/self set against the inescapable fire of lust

beged (garment) — the rhetorical image: 'fire in the bosom' cannot leave the beged unburned. Read honestly as the metaphor-vehicle: the man's own life/self is the garment that illicit desire, held close, is bound to consume. Consequence is inescapable.
